title: Thursday Quick Tip
subtitle: Warm up with a game
hook: Are your players running laps to start practice?
intro: Half the team walks the second one.
statement: A game warms up legs and attention at the same time.
q1: Do you warm up with a tag game or a relay —
q2: or keep a set routine of laps and stretches?
q3: How fast do kids get moving when it is a game?
t1: Every team is different. But warm-ups work better
t2: when kids want to do them.
cta: Coaches — how do you warm up?
ctaLines: Tag. Base-running relays. A ball for everyone.
ctaPrompt: Share your warm-up habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
Are your players running laps to start practice?
Practice starts with two laps. Half the team walks the second one.
A game warms up legs and attention at the same time.
Warm-up games or a set routine. Both can work.
How do you warm up? Share your habit in the comments.
